nodes.Method_Description: Swedana involves heating the raw material in a liquid medium using mild heat, usually by boiling or steaming (often in a Dolayantra setup). The process removes impurities, reduces toxicity, softens the material, and facilitates further purification or processing.

nodes.Preparation: Kanji is prepared by fermenting a mixture of rice (or rice gruel) with water and souring agents (such as mustard or spices) for a specific period until it becomes acidic.
nodes.name: Sour Gruel

nodes.Process_Description: Marana is the calcination of purified metals and minerals through repeated cycles of grinding with herbal media and controlled heating (Puta). This converts the material into fine, ash-like Bhasma that is non-toxic, stable, and bioavailable.
nodes.name: Marana

edges.Result: Shankha Bhasma purified with lemon juice showed significantly higher symptom resolution (66 to 71% vs. 27 to 31%, P < 0.005) and more heartburn-free days, confirming improved therapeutic efficacy after proper Shodhana.

edges.Procedure: Shankha pieces tied in a cloth bundle were boiled in lemon juice for 3 h, then washed with warm water.
Shankha pieces tied in a cloth bundle were boiled in kanji for 3 h, then washed with warm water.
Purified Shankha was sealed in earthen containers and subjected to two cycles of calcination to obtain white Shankha Bhasma.
